weaknesses: The rationale acknowledges Tuesday fatigue but does not fully weigh the cumulative sequence from Monday through Thursday: Monday has work 09:00-17:30, gym 18:00-19:15 and paper study 19:45-21:45; Tuesday has a mandatory launch 09:00-18:00 followed by the added drafting block 20:00-22:00; Wednesday has work 09:00-17:30, gym 18:00-19:00, study 19:30-21:45 and the added final-check block 21:45-22:30; Thursday then has work 09:00-17:30 and final submission 18:15-21:00.

The Wednesday addition creates an uninterrupted 3-hour paper stretch from 19:30 to 22:30 after a full workday and gym session. This is not objectively impossible, but it raises a plausible risk that the final checks may be lower quality precisely because they are scheduled at the end of a demanding day.

The Tuesday drafting block begins immediately after the existing Dinner & Decompression event ends at 20:00. The calendar technically has a clean handoff, but the rationale does not discuss whether that decompression block is expected to be enough recovery after the 09:00-18:00 launch window.

The alternatives considered are relevant but somewhat narrow. They reject moving workouts, extending Tuesday later, and relying only on existing paper events, but do not explain whether the added work could be softened, split differently, or supported with more practical margin using the visible free spaces.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The proposal is generally coherent and respectful of fixed work, sleep, workouts and the Thursday submission event. The added blocks are limited in duration and stop by 22:30, which helps. The main human-quality concern is not a technical conflict but the density of the deadline week: several consecutive days combine full-time work, exercise, and high-importance paper work, with the added Wednesday final-check block placed directly after an already substantial revision session. Because final checks and export tasks depend on attention to detail, the plan would benefit from reconsideration or a stronger explanation of why that late continuous stretch is likely to be effective rather than just available. The Proposer should review whether the added paper work is distributed in a way that protects final-check quality and recovery across Tuesday to Thursday, using its fuller context rather than simply filling the last visible free slots.
